body:
Concurrent child-process launches can leave one worker holding an unrelated worker's stdout pipe write end. After the original worker exits, CREXX waits for output EOF before publishing child completion. The unrelated live worker prevents EOF, delaying completion and downstream worker replacement until it also closes the inherited handle.

This belongs in CREXX's generic process launcher. cREXX-RAG should not need extra monitoring or a pipe workaround.

### Environment

- macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), arm64.
- Installed CREXX `crexx-1.0.0-beta.3+local.g037e7939bc29`, source commit `037e7939bc29eb91b29ed41e9b1b8debdef6353d`.
- Observed in cREXX-RAG's isolated native eight-worker regression fixture, using the child-process channel provider and local synthetic providers. No hosted model or production corpus is required.

### Expected and observed behavior

Each child should retain only its intended redirected streams. Unrelated pipe descriptors must not survive into another executed child. Once worker A exits and its own output is drained, its completion should be delivered while healthy worker B remains alive.

Instead, A's process exit is observed by the runtime, but its output reader remains blocked because B holds a spare writing end of A's pipe. B need not write anything. When the last unrelated holder closes that end, EOF arrives and A's completion can finally be delivered. Healthy peers continue working in the meantime, but the application cannot promptly replace A through its normal completion-driven path.

### Reproduction procedure

The launch timing is intermittent: a focused run passed, and the subsequent full regression run reproduced the delay. A reduced standalone CREXX test has not yet been packaged; the following procedure and descriptor evidence identify the failure without depending on RAG data or a particular model.

1. Open the child-process channel provider (`.channel.open(5, 255, config)`) with capacity 8. Rapidly submit eight `crexx.channel.child-process-start` requests so their launches overlap. Keep the children alive on a local fixture barrier. In the observed application, each request binds stdin/stdout to null byte endpoints and inherits stderr; stdout still uses the runtime's pipe/reader path.
2. Before releasing the children, inspect all child descriptors, for example `lsof -nP -a -p "$worker_pids" -F pftn`, where `worker_pids` is the comma-separated PID list. Find a pipe used as one child's stdout and also held as an extra descriptor in another child. Repeat the launch group if the race did not occur.
3. Kill the original stdout owner with SIGKILL, allowing healthy peers to continue. Observe the dead PID and the controller's child-channel completion events independently.
4. The killed child's completion is delayed while the other process holds its pipe end. Close/terminate that holder; the reader then sees EOF and completion becomes available. If several peers hold the same pipe, all spare writing ends must close.

The downstream test is `ctest --test-dir cmake-build-debug -R '^worker_unexpected_exit$' --output-on-failure`; its current fixture is part of an uncommitted RAG repair, not a reproducer available in the published RAG baseline. It kills a registered worker before or after a locally recorded request intent and checks replacement while seven healthy peers remain alive. The full run hit its replacement observation limit; the killed child's completion appeared during controller drain/peer shutdown.

### Captured descriptor evidence

The isolated native fixture captured these simultaneous handles:

| Process | Descriptor | Pipe endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Worker A, PID 87853 | 1 (stdout) | `->0xf3d72cac815b90c9` |
| Worker B, PID 87854 | 11 (unused inherited handle) | `->0xf3d72cac815b90c9` |
| Worker C, PID 87855 | 1 (stdout) | `->0x66cc65df8c0d3126` |
| Worker D, PID 87856 | 14 | `->0x66cc65df8c0d3126` |
| Worker E, PID 87857 | 14 | `->0x66cc65df8c0d3126` |

The descriptor snapshot establishes cross-worker inheritance. It was a separate diagnostic run from the failing full-suite run; its selected killed worker happened to have an unshared stdout, so that particular replacement completed. This accounts for the launch-order-dependent pass/fail behavior without claiming every recorded run failed.

### Source findings and repair direction

At the installed commit, [`redirect_pipe_start`](https://github.com/adesutherland/CREXX/blob/037e7939bc29eb91b29ed41e9b1b8debdef6353d/interpreter/rxspawn.c#L1395) uses `pipe(handles)`. [`redirect_completion_restrict_child_inheritance`](https://github.com/adesutherland/CREXX/blob/037e7939bc29eb91b29ed41e9b1b8debdef6353d/interpreter/rxspawn.c#L1306) marks only the parent's completion endpoint close-on-exec; the child endpoint remains inheritable. A concurrent launch can inherit that unrelated child endpoint.

The existing [POSIX launch mutex](https://github.com/adesutherland/CREXX/blob/037e7939bc29eb91b29ed41e9b1b8debdef6353d/interpreter/rxspawn.c#L4421) protects the launch-status pipe/fork section, but not redirect-pipe creation and flag setup. The child [duplicates its intended streams](https://github.com/adesutherland/CREXX/blob/037e7939bc29eb91b29ed41e9b1b8debdef6353d/interpreter/rxspawn.c#L4592) without closing unrelated inherited redirect descriptors. After `waitpid` obtains the exit status, the runtime [joins the output reader](https://github.com/adesutherland/CREXX/blob/037e7939bc29eb91b29ed41e9b1b8debdef6353d/interpreter/rxspawn.c#L3794) before publishing completion.

Please apply normal pipe ownership/descriptor cleanup in the generic launcher: prevent unrelated pipe ends surviving exec, while preserving the intended stdin/stdout/stderr redirects. Close-on-exec setup must also avoid a concurrent fork between pipe creation and flag assignment (for example, atomic creation where supported or the existing launch lock around setup). Check both ends and failure cleanup. A regression should prove that killing one child delivers its completion while a sibling remains alive, retaining ordinary output-drain behavior.

No CREXX source has been modified or runtime fix qualified during this investigation. Historical Scottish soak logs alone cannot conclusively attribute every stale worker to this defect. RAG is handing this finding upstream and accepting delayed replacement as a known limitation until the runtime repair is available.
title: POSIX child launches inherit unrelated pipe ends, delaying exit completion until sibling workers close
